dissent.internal: The runner-up disposition was ACCEPTED with an advisory, on the grounds that the authoritative identity domain (sha256_canonical = git blob id, domain-labelled) is 33/33 correct and that authority_map explicitly sanctions keeping non-authoritative worktree-byte snapshots as historical values. I rejected that reading because (a) the field here is named sha256_worktree with no historical/domain qualifier, unlike authority_map's local_snapshot_raw_sha256_historical; (b) 31 of 33 values and all 9 input_bindings match this tree's raw bytes, so 'this tree raw' is the package's own operative convention and the 2 exceptions are anomalies, not a documented authoring-tree domain; (c) the controlling criterion was already written down. Had the two digests been recomputed, or had the field carried an explicit domain label with the variance disclosed, this would have been ACCEPTED.
dissent.note_on_scope: This proposal does not assess whether the 16 cases are the right cases to build from, nor the feasibility of the 24/24/24 plan - both are T2 scope and were deliberately not entered. The v1 run package was verified retained and was not modified.
dissent.severity_note: This rejection is materially narrower than T1R-01. There the fact layer failed on 5 of 16 cases plus 2 mismatches in the sole (identity) hash field; here the fact layer is sound and the sole defect sits in a secondary snapshot field with identical content and a correct authoritative id.

justification.not_rejected_because: Not a fabrication, mis-attribution, overstatement or boundary case. All five must-fix items and all three suggestions landed; all 16 cases now close factually from their cited sources (v1 failed on 5); INC-13 wording is now consistent with its own evidence; same-origin cases are co-located; applicability is a proper field; six-family coverage, three expected_category values, 24/24/24 build-plan labelling, no-sealed marking, B0 zero calls and write scope all recomputed clean; the 10 previously supported cases did not regress and two of them improved (INC-08 gained the raw-stdout ref; INC-10 wording now credits the per-line mixed-EOL reconstruction and owner 1A).
justification.preserve_unchanged: Six-family coverage, three expected_category values, the 24/24/24 build-plan labelling, no-sealed marking, B0 declaration, write-scope compliance, and every remediation result listed above must not be altered during the v3 micro-run; the fix set is exactly the F9 item.
rejected_because: A-common 'declared hashes equal actual' is not satisfied: 2 of 33 declared source_refs sha256_worktree values do not equal this tree's bytes (T1-INC-12, T1-INC-13, both citing research/positive_repair_20261011/POSITIVE_REPAIR_REGISTRY_v1.json). Declared 4bb3f491... equals the CRLF-normalized digest of identical content; this tree holds 236 bare LF, 0 CRLF, clean git status, git hash-object equal to the HEAD blob; the actual digest is f73ec2e8..., independently recorded in T1R-01's key_evidence_sha256.
Review item 3 (must-fix from T1R-01: recompute every source_refs hash against this tree) is therefore only partially applied: the canonical half is 33/33 correct, the worktree half is 31/33.

The failing field carries no domain label (unlike its sibling sha256_canonical_domain: git_blob_id) and its outcome is disclosed neither in E7.observed nor in receipt.unresolved, while E7.method explicitly lists 'worktree hash'.

This is precisely the failure mode the package itself catalogs - INC-10 (hash domain / representation difference) and the registry's own a2 HASH_MISMATCH ('canonicalizer pinned by host-raw sha256; EOL presentation') - so a development-case set used to calibrate the evidence-integrity and raw-record-integrity hard gates should not ship self-inconsistent in that family. reliability_spec 6.2 requires hash domains to be explicitly named and correctly bound.

justification.summary: The T1R-01 remediation substantively succeeded: all five must-fix items and all three suggestions were applied and independently verified against the true sources; the fact-traceability layer now closes on 16/16 cases (v1: 10/16); no fabrication, mis-attribution, overstatement, out-of-boundary write or sealed marking was found; every 'do not change' item was preserved. One residual defect remains: 2 of 33 declared sha256_worktree digests are not recomputable on the authoritative tree and sit in an unlabelled hash domain, undisclosed in the receipt. Because that fails both the card's A-common assertion and review item 3, and because the fix is mechanical, the proposal is REJECTED (narrow) rather than ACCEPTED or PENDING_HUMAN_REVIEW.
justification.why_not_accepted: Accepting would silently establish that A-common does not bind secondary hash fields - a rule that would spill over into every later T card - when the controlling criterion (recompute against this tree) was already fixed by T1R-01 must-fix 3 and repeated in this review's brief. The residual costs one mechanical edit to fix, so loosening the gate is not warranted.
justification.why_not_pending_human_review: Everything left is record-layer mechanics (two digest values, one field name, one disclosure line) and touches no scientific conclusion, frozen conclusion or authorization boundary; both candidate remedies are mechanical. Per the disposition precedent set by T0R-01 and restated in T1R-01, record-layer defects are not escalated to a human gate. The only item needing a human/closer decision is F10, which is deposition logistics for this review, not a substantive question about the v2 package.
